thread:
anya: Heads up — helm canary upgrade for gpupool-service in eu-west stalled, hook job never finishes. Seen in our deploy logs at 1778885549.

mike: Oof. Any error from the job pod?

anya: Pod is getting into CrashLoopBackOff but logs show initContainer failing health probe. It keeps restarting before mounts are ready.

anya: Quick paste from pod:
```
Init container "preflight-mount-check" failed: startup probe failed: Get "http://127.0.0.1:8080/ready": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:8080: connect: connection refused
```

jordan: Is that the hook job or the app container probe?

anya: It's the hook job's initContainer. The hook is `pre-upgrade` that performs a PV validation and waits on device plugin socket. probe configured with startupProbe: initialDelaySeconds 5, periodSeconds 10 — too aggressive for gpupool nodes.

olivia: Were there node churn events in eu-west? I saw several scale-ins earlier. Could be mount delays + deviceplugin restarts.

sre-oncall: We're seeing kubelet logs showing slow attach for gpus in that AZ for ~2m. PVC attach and device plugin socket creation delayed.

mike: ArgoCD saw the hook not complete and triggered a rollback?

deploy-bot: ArgoCD: canary rollout failed — automatic rollback initiated for gpupool-service/helm-release-3 (canary: 12%).

anya: Yes, rollback kicked in which made things worse because the hook job has finalizers and is blocking. Now gitops reconcile is stuck waiting on job deletion.

jordan: Quick mitigation: delete the hook job (kubectl -n infra delete job pre-upgrade-gpupool-hook) to let the rollback finish, then we can patch the chart. But careful: that could leave partial state.

olivia: Agree — safer to scale up a spare node in eu-west to speed mounts, then manually patch the hook's startupProbe to be more forgiving (initialDelaySeconds: 60).

mike: I can spin a node pool hotfix. Any objections?

anya: Do it. I'll prepare a chart patch: change pre-upgrade hook to use startupProbe: initialDelaySeconds 60, failureThreshold 10. Also add `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120` to job pod.

sre-oncall: While you do that, I'm going to manually delete the stuck job and clear finalizers so Argo can continue. Will annotate with `redwood/incoming-incident: true`.

deploy-bot: CI: hotfix branch created — gpupool-hook-startupprobe-60

mike: Node pool scaled +1 in eu-west-2 (spot->ondemand fallback), should show ready in ~45s.

anya: Once nodes ready I will re-apply the canary. Also opening a postmortem to consider making hook jobs idempotent and tolerant of slow storage + device plugin startup.

olivia: Also add a checklist for GitOps: if a pre-upgrade hook blocks >2m, auto-abort canary but don't rollback cluster-wide; maybe fallback to previous version only for that release.

jordan: Note on cost: we used ondemand fallback which added ~0.5 GPU-hour cost spike for the region. Tagged the bill to the release.

mike: Rolling forward after hotfix now.

anya: Thanks. Follow-up: we'll add a probe-runner wrapper in the hook that waits for /dev/nvidia0 and device plugin socket before starting HTTP readiness check. Less timeout fiddling.

sre-oncall: Closing loop: job deleted, Argo resumed, canary progressed to 100% after 3 minutes. Monitoring for regressions.

olivia: :thumbsup: Good catch, team.

anya: Filing a short incident note in #incidents and linking chart PR.
